Note that your refactoring here runs both tests within a single app_context as the fixture teardown isn't executed until you exist the test function. Versus the previous way used separate app contexts. I don't think it matters in this case, although I'm uncertain as it's been a while since I've looked at what `app_context()` is actually doing.

You might consider refactoring this using `pytest` parameterization. Pass the test function `True`/`False` for `JSON_AS_ASCII` as well as the expected output. This would also stay within the original behavior of creating a new app context each run through.

I reviewed this when I rewrote the tutorial, `mkstemp()` still seemed to be the easiest way to handle this in these tests. If we're going to change this, I'd rather use pytest's `tmp_path` fixture, but I think I tried that last time and couldn't find a satisfying solution.

This doesn't call `f.close()`, but tests need to clean up after themselves. You'd need to wrap the entire function in a `with` block. I didn't do that because it just pushed the indentation level out.

This is also making all the tests fail, because `TemporaryFile` does not create a visible name. You'd want `NamedTemporaryFile` in that case.
